CETA (Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, and FINTRAC regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, ss. 462.31 and 83.03; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 13; Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, Part 21.2 (Individuals with Significant Control register), as amended by the Business Corporations Amendment Act, 2024; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44 (if federal incorporation elected).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or registered agent of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 HCCH Convention; in force for Canada since January 11, 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies of all directors, officers, and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Contracting States, consular legalization at the Canadian visa office

Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign registrar or corporate registry of the parent shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter supporting aviation escrow and SWIFT wire payment rails

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every director, officer, UBO, and affiliated corporate entity against FINTRAC administrative requirements, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, and domestic PEP registries with open-source adverse media review. Continuous enhanced monitoring is required for the aviation spares distribution sector under the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier, including transaction-level screening of all escrow and SWIFT wire counterparties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) via authorized service providers through the MyAlberta Business Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed corporate names must consist of English or French words, numerals, or Roman-script letters; transliterations from non-Roman scripts must be submitted and registered only in Roman form. Names must comply with Alberta's name regulation and must not be misleading, falsely imply government/royal patronage, or be confusingly similar to existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A fresh NUANS name search report is required after the 90-day window; no extension is available. Upon name rejection, the applicant must file a written reconsideration request with the Director of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry, within 30 days of the rejection notice, attaching the NUANS report, explanatory submissions, and any ministerial consent letters. If the Director maintains the refusal, judicial review may be pursued before the Alberta Court of King's Bench under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSA 2000, c J-3.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible under section 101 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act, which requires a registered office address in Alberta. For aviation spares distribution and to satisfy banking KYC at the Medium_Risk_Enhanced tier, a physical operational site (warehouse or office) is strongly recommended; virtual-office-only structures are generally rejected by major banks and aviation escrow counterparties.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified unannounced physical inspection probability of 35% per annum for enhanced-distribution EPC activities, reflecting CRA, Alberta municipal business licensing, and Transport Canada oversight norms.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended, applicable provisions including Part 1 (Incorporation and Articles), section 10 (Corporate Name), section 11 (Directions to Authorized Service Providers), Part 3 (Directors and Officers), Part 5 (Shares and Share Certificates), Part 6 (Registered Office and Records), and Schedule 1 (Forms); supporting regulations under the Alberta Corporate Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, operating through Government of Alberta authorized Corporation Service Providers and the Corporate Registry Online system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation together with Notice of Registered Office, Consent to Act as Director, and related statutory schedules filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed under the Alberta Business Corporations Act. The articles may authorize shares with a nominal paid-up amount, commonly CAD 100.00 divided among founding subscribers. No escrow account is required by the province for a general distribution company; escrow arrangements apply only where contractually required or under a regulated aviation financing or other special regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator's subscription for 100 common shares in the capital of the Corporation, at CAD $100 per share, is accepted; the shares are allotted and issued as fully paid; the Secretary is directed to record issuance in the register of members. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Corporation in Alberta is established at [address], and its registered office records shall be filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each until successors are elected; the officers are authorized to complete statutory filings, open bank accounts, and obtain licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta — NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) through authorized service providers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed corporate name for a NUANS search; review the search report against existing Alberta and federal trade-marks and corporate names; reserve an acceptable name for 90 days; ensure the name contains a proper legal element such as Inc. or Corp. and does not include prohibited terms. For a surplus aircraft parts distributor, avoid terms suggesting regulated carriers unless relevant approvals are held.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name
NUANS search request and fee receipt
Authorized applicant instruction or corporate service provider engagement
Contact details of the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusingly similar, obtain legal opinion, amend the name to include a distinguishing trade-mark or descriptive element, and resubmit for a further NUANS search; alternatively adopt a numbered company name and file a Name Change Amendment after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or corporate governing agent acting under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; notarization accepted where required for non-resident directors or officers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation prescribing the class and maximum number of shares, restrictions on share transfers, and any special voting provisions. Prepare By-law No. 1, the registered office notice, director consents, and initial subscription agreements. Ensure the business purpose includes wholesale distribution of certified civil aviation rotables, avionics, and surplus aircraft parts. Execute all documents under hand or by notarized signature where requested.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation
Notice of Registered Office and address for service in Alberta
Consent to Act as Director for each director
By-law No. 1 (organizational by-law)
Initial share subscription agreement and capital book
Incorporator's declaration and identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise and re-execute the defective document; if the registry queries director consent, obtain a fresh signed consent from an eligible substitute director and resubmit within 30 days; correct by-law or article defects through a supplementary filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta — Corporate Registry Online or authorized Corporation Service Provider.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed Articles of Incorporation, Notice of Registered Office, Consent to Act as Director, and NUANS report to the Alberta Corporate Registry; pay the prescribed filing fee using an approved payment method; obtain the corporate file number and acknowledgement. The application will be reviewed for completeness, statutory compliance, and absence of prohibited names.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Incorporation
Valid NUANS name search report no older than 90 days
Notice of Registered Office
Consent to Act as Director for each director
Filing fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the technical deficiency and resubmit under the same corporate file number where possible; if the name reservation lapses, procure a fresh NUANS report and refile; if articles are rejected, file amended articles with the registry before the next business day cutoff to avoid additional fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta — Registry Service Desk and Certificate Issuance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following approval, download the official Certificate of Incorporation and corporate access number from the registry system; confirm the legal name, jurisdiction, corporate number, and effective date; print and place the certificate in the corporate minute book; obtain the Corporate Access Number for future electronic filings and the Alberta Business Registry account.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Alberta Corporate Registry
Corporate Access Number confirmation
Corporate Registry record of current registered office and directors
Minute book organizational paper
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical error, file a Statement of Correction under the ABCA; if the certificate is misplaced, request a certified copy from Service Alberta; if the registered office address is inaccurate, file a Notice of Change of Registered Office as a curative step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Industrial, and Aviation Licensing Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Alberta Labour Immigration and Workplace Safety, Workers' Compensation Board Alberta, Transport Canada Civil Aviation, and applicable municipal business licensing authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the corporate Business Number with the Canada Revenue Agency; apply for GST/HST and payroll accounts concurrently; register with the Workers' Compensation Board for workplace coverage; obtain a municipal business licence for the physical premises; if engaging directly in regulated aviation parts activities, file the required registration/notification with Transport Canada Civil Aviation for aircraft component distribution traceability and maintain part certification records in accordance with Canadian Aviation Regulations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number
CRA Business Number registration form
Proof of registered office and physical operations address
Director and officer identification records
Commercial lease or ownership document for the warehouse/office
Fire safety and municipal zoning clearance
Workers' Compensation Board industrial classification information
Aviation part traceability and certification procedures manual where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For CRA registration delays, contact the Business Registration Telephone Service; for Workers' Compensation Board reclassification, submit revised industrial class information and payroll estimates; for municipal licensing refusal, appeal under the Municipal Government Act or relocate to an appropriately zoned area; for Transport Canada queries, supplement the traceability manual and certification evidence and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Labour, Immigration and Workplace Safety, Industrial and Occupational Licensing Division, in coordination with Transport Canada Civil Aviation and the applicable Alberta municipal business licensing authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Alberta General Industrial Distribution Operating Licence and Aviation Component Distribution Operational Clearance for Certified Civil Aircraft Rotables and Avionics Surplus under Canadian Aviation Regulations Part I, Subpart 1 and Alberta occupational licensing requirements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration under Schedule B of the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, Alberta, as a lower-risk warehousing and distribution operation; full Environmental Impact Assessment report not required absent significant emissions, hazardous waste generation, or fuel storage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives including VOC emission limits; prohibition on unauthorized liquid effluent discharge to stormwater or municipal sewers under the Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act Wastewater and Storm Drainage Regulation; proper handling, labelling, and disposal of used aircraft fluids, batteries, and hazardous surplus components under the Waste Control Regulation; spill containment and secondary containment for any stored lubricants or chemicals.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Completion of a fire safety inspection and certification under the Alberta Fire Code and municipal fire by-laws, including emergency exits, extinguishers, and alarm systems; structural load inspections for warehouse racking and storage mezzanines; workplace health and safety clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act and Code; and municipal zoning and business licence approval confirming permitted commercial use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO) portal; Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) - Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS); Alberta Corporate Registry for extra-provincial registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Canadian corporation obtains a 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) immediately after federal or Alberta incorporation. With respect to a non-resident corporation, apply via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or the applicable non-resident request form. Open the required program accounts: 0001 (Corporation Income Tax), RT (GST/HST), RC (payroll), and RM (import/export). Complete the Alberta extra-provincial registration under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). GST/HST registration becomes mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or across the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters; a non-resident making taxable supplies in Canada must register unless it qualifies as a small supplier or the goods are delivered through a carrier or consignee exception.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box regime and no elective hybrid-mismatch regime; entity classification is statutory. A Canadian-incorporated Business Corporation is a resident taxpayer under section 2(2) of the Income Tax Act (Canada) and is taxed on worldwide income. Available elections relevant to a distributing corporation include: the Excise Tax Act section 156 election between closely related registrants to render inter-corporate supplies of goods and services not subject to GST/HST; the joint election under section 167(1) of the Excise Tax Act for certain supplies of goods and real property; and the Income Tax Act section 249.1 election for a non-calendar-year taxation year in limited first-year circumstances. Draft OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid-mismatch rules, if enacted, will operate as mandatory provisions and do not create elective relief.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST). Alberta applies the federal 5% GST only; there is no Harmonized Sales Tax and no Alberta provincial sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold under section 148(1) of the Excise Tax Act, measured on worldwide gross taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter or over the four preceding consecutive calendar quarters; non-residents making taxable supplies in Canada must register once the threshold is exceeded, subject to the carrier-delivery exception.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API invoice clearance, or digital stamping mandate exists under federal or Alberta law. Electronic invoices are permitted where they satisfy the record-keeping and information requirements of sections 236 and 237 of the Excise Tax Act. GST/HST registrants must file returns electronically via GST NETFILE; export declarations are submitted electronically through the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) using the prescribed export declaration format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of surplus certified commercial aircraft rotables, avionics, and parts qualify for zero-rating under subsection 22(1) of the Excise Tax Act and Schedule VI where the vendor exports the tangible personal property as part of a contract of sale, ships or delivers the goods to a destination outside Canada by common carrier, or the non-resident recipient exports the goods as part of the sale within the prescribed period. The vendor must retain prescribed documentary evidence within the two-year evidence window for exported goods; otherwise the supply is subject to 5% GST and any claimed input tax credits or refunds are subject to reassessment and clawback.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canadian Export Declaration (CERS/G13 electronic export report or Form B13A) evidencing the export of goods valued over CAD 2,000 or controlled consignments

Commercial invoice with Tax Code 0 zero-rated GST/HST statement, full export description, and airworthiness documentation (FAA 8130-3, EASA Form 1, or Transport Canada AFM) for certified aircraft parts
Bill of Lading, House Air Waybill, or Master Air Waybill evidencing delivery to a named foreign destination and the consignee's foreign address
Packing list and Cargo Control Document (CCD) or house manifest with export shipment identifier
Destination-country customs entry or import clearance record confirming receipt of the parts outside Canada, where available
Inward remittance certificate, SWIFT wire confirmation, or bank settlement record evidencing foreign-currency repatriation of export proceeds within the 180-day deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and CBSA may jointly audit the entire export chain, from purchase and inventory to foreign delivery and payment settlement. Failure to produce the prescribed export documents converts an allegedly zero-rated export into a taxable supply at 5% GST, triggering reassessment within the normal four-year limitation period or without time limit in cases of misrepresentation, negligence, or fraud. Input tax credits and refunds are clawed back with statutory interest. Civil penalties include the false-statement penalty of the greater of CAD 500 and 50% of the tax sought to be evaded under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act, plus penalties for false Customs Act export declarations. Criminal prosecution under sections 326 and 327 of the Excise Tax Act and section 239 of the Income Tax Act may result in fines of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to five years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with foreign exchange administration exercised through the Financial Administration Act, the Currency Act, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); FINTRAC serves as the financial intelligence and transaction reporting authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible. Both current account transactions and capital account transactions are generally free from exchange control restrictions. There are no blocked-fund rules preventing the repatriation of dividends, interest, royalties, or liquidation proceeds. The principal remittance hurdle is non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, typically 25%, reducible under applicable tax treaties, together with Form NR4 reporting and remittance obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender obligation and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may retain foreign currency receipts in offshore or domestic foreign-currency accounts without restriction. Transactions involving foreign currency equivalent to CAD 10,000 or more, and all international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, must be reported to FINTRAC under the PCMLTFA.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Corporate Account
Operational Account / Trade Finance and Escrow Account
Operational Account / International Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium as a primary operating account and Medium as an ancillary collection or disbursement channel. An offshore electronic money institution (EMI) is not authorized to take deposits in Canada under the Bank Act and may not function as the principal settlement account for a Canadian corporate treasury. Unless the offshore EMI has a proper Canadian nexus, it may need to be registered as a foreign money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC. For high-value surplus aircraft parts transactions under escrow, a Schedule I Canadian chartered bank account is strongly preferred and usually required by counterparties, airframe manufacturers, and title escrow agents.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian Schedule I banks generally require at least one signing director, officer, or authorized banking attorney to attend an identity-verification interview before a corporate account is fully activated. Remote video-KYC and digital onboarding are increasingly available, but for a newly formed Alberta business corporation with non-resident ultimate beneficial owners, one principal is normally required to appear physically at a Canadian branch or before a notary public acceptable to the bank. The bank must verify the corporate existence, registered address, directors, and every ultimate beneficial owner with 25% or more control before an account mandate is executed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound funds transfers from a foreign aviation surplus broker combined with a recently appointed shareholder or layered corporate ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Alberta incorporation; corporate by-laws and director/shareholder resolutions appointing account signatories; full register of directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs); source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations; executed surplus parts purchase and sale agreements; aircraft parts traceability package including Transport Canada, FAA, or EASA certification documents; bank references from the counterparty's KYC file; and a sworn statement explaining the commercial rationale for the transaction routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or through third-party intermediaries, especially to US Florida or UAE free-zone brokers, with a request for same-day USD conversion and onward settlement outside Canada.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A clear transaction flow chart identifying all intermediaries; written tripartite escrow instructions; original commercial invoice and air waybill; customs entry documentation under Canadian and US regulations; FAA 8130-3 or EASA Form 1 airworthiness certificates; end-user certificate or reseller undertaking; OFAC and sanctions screening reports for all parties; evidence of arm's length pricing; and an undertaking to maintain records under PCMLTFA, FINTRAC, and the bank's enhanced due diligence requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible or aircraft spare parts dual-use risk flagged during sanctions screening because of jurisdiction exposure or on-board consignee information.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Harmonized System classification and Canadian Export Control List analysis; inline embargo and restricted-party compliance certificate; transport documentation confirming the physical goods route from Canada to a permitted destination; bill of lading with exact commodity description and serial numbers; security-control authorizations; original purchase order from the certified end user; legal opinion on the absence of controlled-goods classification; and evidence that the intended use is civil aviation spare-parts distribution only.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with the Canadian institution and transit numbers, beneficiary SWIFT BIC, and the beneficiary account at a Schedule I Canadian bank. In the remittance information field, clearly state 'Paid-up capital contribution to Alberta business corporation' or 'Shareholder loan disbursement' as applicable. The bank will require the certificate of incorporation, directors' register, and account mandate. All international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more are reported to FINTRAC. Funds must originate from the direct account of the shareholder or beneficial owner; pooled third-party processors are not acceptable for equity injections, and the bank may request a legal entity identifier (LEI) for the corporate shareholder.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic CAD payment obligations are cleared through the Canadian Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for high-value transactions and through the Retail Payment System for smaller payments. Cross-border trade disbursements to US and international suppliers use SWIFT MT103, commercial letters of credit, or documentary collections. For surplus commercial aircraft parts, settlement rails are typically 'Escrow_Aviation' and 'SWIFT Wire': payment is released only after presentation and verification of title documentation, airworthiness certificates, and inspection reports. USD payments can be cleared through the Canadian bank's US-dollar clearing hub or a US correspondent bank using ABA routing and Fedwire; CAD/USD conversions are executed at the same-day commercial bank rate with FX confirmation matching the underlying invoice.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable plain-vanilla over-the-counter FX forwards under bilateral ISDA/IFEMA documentation with a Canadian chartered bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid currencies where physical settlement is unavailable
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge long-term shareholder loan and USD trade settlement exposures
European-style FX options on major currency pairs under commercially reasonable bank credit limits
CME or Montreal Exchange listed Canadian dollar/US dollar futures and options for transparent exchange-traded hedging
Structural FX swap arrangements to align Canadian-dollar inflows with USD disbursement cycles and dividend repatriation timing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) or Extra-Provincial Registration Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of CAD 50 if filed after 60 days; failure to file for two consecutive years can lead to administrative dissolution or cancellation of extra-provincial registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), if federally incorporated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No regulatory late fee is prescribed, but failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Director to dissolve the corporation administratively under section 212 of the CBCA

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and Alberta Corporate Income Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 6 months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax, plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeat failures incur an additional penalty of 10%; CRA interest and criminal prosecution apply for willful non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return, if registered and an annual filing period applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 3 months after the end of the corporation's fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the amount owing, plus 1% per month up to 12 months; daily interest accrues on unpaid amounts; deemed failure may result in mandatory accelerated filing frequency

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold triggers a mandatory private company audit under the CBCA or the Alberta Business Corporations Act. A private corporation may waive the appointment of an auditor each year by unanimous shareholder consent; a public or distributing corporation must appoint an independent auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises; private corporations may elect to use IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO filing is made to any registry. The individuals with significant control (ISC) register must be maintained at the registered office and updated within 15 days after becoming aware of any change. Annual returns report registered directors and registered members; they do not require disclosure of underlying significant individuals. Share transfers must be reflected in the Register of Members and in the register of individuals with significant control where applicable.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control
